learning_outcomes.text: Address the complete implementation of an “embedded system” based on microprocessors and/or microcontrollers in their professional life.
Fluently handle the datasheets of typical electronic components of embedded systems: microprocessors, microcontrollers, and peripheral integrated circuits.
Connect various devices (memories, I/O controllers, etc.) with a microprocessor and/or microcontroller according to their needs and given specifications.

Understand the characteristics of microcontrollers, establish their field of application, and select the most suitable microcontroller for a given application, from technical and economic points of view.
Know the programming language for a specific microprocessor/microcontroller, and use the most common development tools: assembler, compilers, simulators, emulators, etc., that facilitate development.
Work in a group, reason critically to compare different solutions and discriminate the most optimal one.
Acquire the ability to solve open problems and projects through analysis and information search. Defend their solution against other possible ones using oral communication.
Use A/D and D/A conversion circuits, both discrete and integrated into microcontrollers or other devices.
Design and implement digital systems using timer blocks, A/D and D/A converters integrated into microcontrollers, and select the optimal one for each application.
Know and use the most common digital communication buses and standards between systems (RS-232, RS-485, etc.) and between integrated circuits (SPI, I2C, etc.).
Manage and design complex I/O circuits and interfaces, such as LCDs and their associated circuits, both at a logical and electrical level.

Use programmable logic devices as another component within electronic design, distinguishing when their use is advantageous over other alternatives and managing their various debugging and development tools for a given family.

syllabus_topics: Operation of a minimum microprocessor system
teaching_methods: Classroom practical sessions for exercise and problem solving

assessment_methods.method: Activities in Class (ACE) for Laboratory Block

assessment_rules: The final grade is calculated as 30% Laboratory (LAB) and 70% Theory (TEORIA). A minimum score of 4 out of 10 is required in both the Laboratory and Theory blocks. If both minimums are met, the final grade is 0.3*LAB + 0.7*TEORIA, with a minimum of 5 to pass. If either block scores less than 4, the final grade will be the minimum of 4 or the weighted sum (0.3*LAB + 0.7*TEORIA). For extraordinary calls, the laboratory block grade can be maintained if it was above 4, or a personal work or final exam will be conducted. The theory block grade will include the partial exams (30%) and a final theory exam (70%).
